PEP 695 type aliases (`type Kind = int`) resolve: importing one is the object
import it always was, not a `CP002`.

### Fixed

- The first-party binder had no `ast.TypeAlias` case, so a module binding
  only type aliases looked like it bound nothing, and every import of such a
  name — a package `__init__.py`'s re-export included — was reported `CP002`
  ("could not determine whether ... is a module or an object") rather than
  the `CP001` an object import is. A `type` statement now binds its name as
  an object exactly as a `class` of that name does, with the same treatment
  under conditionals, in function bodies, and against a same-named submodule
  on disk.

Full details: [CHANGELOG.md, 0.6.0](https://github.com/grAItools/cleanporter/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#060---2026-10-07)
